Get started with inmetr

Source: vignettes/articles/inmetr.Rmd
inmetr.Rmd

inmetr reads hourly and daily observations from INMET’s automatic weather stations. The data run from 2000 to February 2025. Each table is split into one Parquet file per year. inmetr downloads only the years you ask for and queries them with DuckDB, so you filter and summarise with dplyr before anything enters memory.

library(inmetr)
library(dplyr)

Find a station

Most municipalities have no station of their own. inmet_nearest() ranks stations by their distance to a municipality seat. It accepts an IBGE code or a name, and accents and case don’t matter.

poa <- inmet_nearest("Porto Alegre", n = 3)
poa |>
  select(code_station, name_station, status, name_muni, distance_km)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   code_station name_station                   status    name_muni    distance_km
#>   <chr>        <chr>                          <chr>     <chr>              <dbl>
#> 1 A801         Porto Alegre - Jardim Botanico operating Porto Alegre        5.91
#> 2 B807         Porto Alegre- Belem Novo       operating Porto Alegre       18.2 
#> 3 A884         Campo Bom                      operating Campo Bom          42.4

A name shared by several municipalities is an error. Pass state to choose one:

inmet_nearest("Bom Jesus")
#> Error in `inmet_nearest()`:
#> ! Ambiguous `muni` "Bom Jesus". Matches: Bom Jesus/PI (2201903), Bom
#>   Jesus/RN (2401701), Bom Jesus/PB (2502201), Bom Jesus/SC (4202537), Bom
#>   Jesus/RS (4302303), Bom Jesus/GO (5203500). Use `state` or an IBGE code.
inmet_nearest("Bom Jesus", state = "RS") |>
  select(code_station, name_station, distance_km)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   code_station name_station          distance_km
#>   <chr>        <chr>                       <dbl>
#> 1 A829         Sao Jose Dos Ausentes        37.9

inmet_stations() returns the full station table. Closed stations stay in it with status = "closed", and first_obs and last_obs show what period each station covers.

inmet_stations() |>
  count(status)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   status        n
#>   <chr>     <int>
#> 1 broken       97
#> 2 closed       50
#> 3 operating   469

Query daily data

read_inmet() returns a lazy table. The years argument controls which files are downloaded, and dplyr verbs build a SQL query that DuckDB runs when you call collect().

daily <- read_inmet("daily", years = 2020:2024)

monthly <- daily |>
  filter(code_station == "A801", !is.na(temp_mean_c), n_hours >= 18) |>
  group_by(year, month) |>
  summarise(
    temp_mean_c = mean(temp_mean_c),
    n_days = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, month) |>
  collect()
#> Warning: Missing values are always removed in SQL aggregation functions.
#> Use `na.rm = TRUE` to silence this warning
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.

monthly
#> # A tibble: 60 × 4
#>     year month temp_mean_c n_days
#>    <int> <int>       <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1  2020     1        25.3     31
#>  2  2020     2        24.8     29
#>  3  2020     3        24.5     31
#>  4  2020     4        20.4     30
#>  5  2020     5        16.8     31
#>  6  2020     6        16.5     30
#>  7  2020     7        13.7     31
#>  8  2020     8        16.1     31
#>  9  2020     9        16.9     30
#> 10  2020    10        19.3     31
#> # ℹ 50 more rows

inmetr publishes INMET’s values without outlier filtering or coverage thresholds, so choose a coverage rule that suits your analysis. The query above keeps days with a mean temperature and at least 18 hours of data, and n_days reports how many days each month retains. n_hours counts hours with at least one valid measurement of any variable, so it doesn’t guarantee 18 hours of temperature readings. For variable-specific coverage, count non-missing values in the hourly table.

The daily table aggregates the hourly one by local standard date. For sub-daily questions, use read_inmet("hourly", years = ...) the same way. Timestamps there are in UTC, and date_local and hour_local give the station’s local standard time.

Cache

Files go to inmet_cache_dir() on first use. inmetr checks each downloaded Parquet file against the SHA-256 hash listed in the release manifest and reuses cached files after that. inmet_cache_clear() deletes the cached release.
